reuse.why: Fintegra goes through linkBankSyncAccount, findOrCreateBank and the existing Akahu balance branch in processBankSyncDownload, but the unlink reset repeats unlinkAccount's and the download function copies Akahu's.

duplication.why: unlinkReplacedAccounts repeats unlinkAccount's eight-field reset, downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, and the same assert-then-forward block is pasted into six provider wrappers.

placement.why: linkBankSyncAccount already receives source, externalAccountId, upgradingId and (via LinkAccountBaseParams) replaceExistingLink, yet the check runs in each wrapper and its result is threaded back in as replacedIds; the new helpers also land under the comment that documents linkBankSyncAccount.

scope.why: Every edit serves one of the four steps, with release notes and tests.

maintainability.why: A new provider must remember to call assertBankAccountNotLinked and pass replacedIds; an 'assert' that returns ids to mutate and also checks closed accounts is easy to misuse.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six provider links call assertBankAccountNotLinked and linkBankSyncAccount; nothing goes around them.

disguised_duplication.where: The copied reset (unlinkReplacedAccounts) and the Fintegra download are literal copies, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gained replacedIds (unlinked in both of its branches); assertBankAccountNotLinked gained replaceExistingLink and carries a closed-account branch alongside the duplicate check.
